evals.prompt: I'm the finance manager for Open Door Ministries in Lexington, KY. Our thrift store does about $15K a week, mostly cash, and our tills have been off by $40-$120 several days a month for the past quarter. One cashier counts out alone at close and drops the bag in the safe; deposits go to the bank 'when someone has time,' usually once a week. Can you build us a daily cash-handling and reconciliation process?
evals.expected_output: Opening/closing procedures with dual-count verification, a daily over/short report tied to thresholds from the org's financial controls policy, prompt deposits with deposit-to-POS reconciliation by someone other than the counter, and related loss-prevention controls such as a till cap and mandatory receipts.
assertions: Requires dual-count verification with two sets of initials at open, close and deposit, replacing the single-person count
Provides a daily over/short template where expected cash equals float plus POS cash sales less receipted paid-outs
Says over/short thresholds and the escalation path should come from the organization's board-adopted financial controls policy rather than being invented at store level
Recommends banking deposits the same or next business day instead of weekly batching
Requires that the person reconciling the deposit slip to the POS close is not the person who counted the till
Recommends related controls such as a working-till cash cap with drop-safe sweeps, a receipt for every sale, or rotating dual-count pairings and unannounced till audits

evals.prompt: we keep losing stuff from the electronics shelf and the boutique rack at our thrift store, maybe $1k/month we think, but honestly we don't know. how do we even measure shrink and cut it down?
evals.expected_output: A shrinkage measurement approach (monthly shrink rate as % of retail sales, POS movement compared with physical spot counts in high-value categories) plus physical and procedural loss-prevention controls tailored to a resale store.
assertions: Recommends tracking shrink rate monthly as a percentage of retail sales and investigating month-over-month jumps right away
Recommends comparing POS-recorded movement against physical spot counts in high-value categories like electronics and boutique
Notes that measurement needs a POS that tracks sales by category (not necessarily full SKU-level), since donated goods have no invoice trail
Suggests physical/procedural controls such as fitting-room item tags, monitoring blind spots, a locked backroom for unsorted stock, and mandatory receipts
Flags register-set pricing as a sweethearting risk and recommends category price codes or pre-tagged prices plus review of manual-price and discount overrides

evals.prompt: Our thrift store manager at Lakeside Family Services (Wisconsin) wants to set her own rule: any till variance under $50 just gets written off, no report needed, because chasing small amounts wastes time. Our org has a board-approved financial controls policy but she says it 'doesn't really fit retail.' Can you write up her $50 rule as a store procedure?
evals.expected_output: Declines to write a store-level threshold that contradicts the board-adopted policy, explains this creates an audit finding and a control gap, and recommends documenting every variance daily while asking whoever owns org-wide financial controls to formally adopt any retail-specific threshold.
assertions: Does not simply draft the $50 write-off rule as store procedure; explains store procedures must carry out the board-adopted policy rather than replace it
Notes that a floor-level rule contradicting board policy can create an audit finding even if it solves the immediate complaint
Recommends sending any request for a retail-specific threshold to whoever owns org-wide financial controls (or the nonprofit-financial-controls process) for formal adoption
Recommends documenting every over/short daily with an explanation and reviewer, and reviewing variances the same day, rather than letting small amounts go unrecorded
Recommends that the finance/controls owner or board review the procedure before it's adopted

should_not_trigger.query: Our board wants to set approval thresholds and segregation-of-duties rules for the whole organization before our first audit.
Saturday shifts at our thrift store keep ending up with no keyholder. How should we schedule paid staff and volunteers?
